claims.claim: The blink ability provides a fifteen meter, silent, invisible, and infinitely rechargeable teleport that allows bypassing obstacles completely.

citations.review_text:
Dishonored is extraordinarily bad. I'm astonished that this is considered a hallmark of stealth imsim hybrids, but describing what about this game doesn't work is really hard to do exhaustively in a steam review. However, the single largest problem here is actually really easy to find.

In short, every obstacle in this game can be solved completely and easily AND FREELY by using blink, which wouldn't be fine even if that ability was some ultra-secret-endgame-side-quest-reward, but you're given it for [u]FREE[/u] as part of the tutorial. One easy payment of three runes later and you have hands down the most broken power I've ever seen in any game. Who thought that a fifteen meter, silent, invisible, infinitely rechargeable, usable while carrying bodies, auto ledge climbing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ [b][i]TELEPORT[/i][/b] was a good idea in a stealth immersive sim??? Am I missing something?????????

bad game

A 2012 game that proved stealth-action could be elegant instead of exhausting, and twelve years later it still holds up better than most "immersive sims" that came after it trying to copy the formula. Dishonored doesn't waste time — it trusts players to figure out their own approach instead of hand-holding through branching narrative trees, and that restraint is exactly why it works.

The PC version runs cleaner than the console originals (360 version had janky performance, PS4 remaster smoothed it out), but the core design transcends platform. The genius is the level design: every environment is built to support multiple solutions. A rooftop path, a sewage tunnel, the front door, possession chains, rat swarms — the game doesn't care how you solve its problems, just that you solve them. This is real player agency, not the false choice trees that most games pretend is depth.

The dark, industrial art direction holds up completely. The magic system feels deliberate and weighty — using a power costs something (mana, noise, your cover), so every ability feels like a tactical choice rather than a freebie spam button. The story is thin (revenge plot, some plot twists that land, some that don't), but it's deliberately thin — the narrative steps back and lets the world breathe instead of constantly narrating your journey.

Even replaying this after PS4 and 360 versions, the core mechanics still feel right. It's a masterclass in level design that doesn't feel dated because it wasn't trying to be cutting-edge — it was trying to be smart. The sequels got bogged down in scope; the original just nailed the fundamentals.

Essential stealth-action game that aged gracefully. Get it on sale if you haven't already.

claims.claim: The game features a morality and chaos system where killing enemies leads to darker story endings, changes in character dialogue, and increased difficulty with more guards and enemies.

citations.review_text:
Pros and Cons since I have started playing (MIGHT HAVE SOME SPOILER HINTS SO READ WITH CAUTION)

Pros:
Great storyline, really well made choice based interactions, combat is fun, lots of mechanics that add to the game in a beneficial way.

Cons:
Despite being an assassin type game, you are punished for assassinating, which is the one thing that made me return this game. I thought the whole point was to get through missions in a way of your choice, explore the lore and have fun exploring different mechanics and interesting various ways to take down enemies as an assassin, but apparently you are punished with far harder enemies, darker storyline endings, and general relationships with even your allies turning for the worse.

Summary: If you are looking for a game that challenges your decisions and like to explore various story endings along with great story and character development then this game is definitely for you. If you prefer not having to worry about hidden mechanics that make gameplay involuntarily harder from enemies and allies alike in the game despite being what you are supposed and asked to be, then its better to search for another game, possibly have this game in your library as a trophy of sorts.

Only the ending amused me.

I spend each mission on high chaos and in most of them, my hp was lower than 10 at all times. Apparently you were suppose to gather health potion by checking every nock and cranny of each building. I found that to be a huge hassle. Many times i was in the mentality of "Just get this mission over with" because it got that insufferable to deal with. Every time i fight someone, at least in the early game, my hp would drop like crazy and i would have no healing potions nor ammunition whatsoever.

God forbid i get stuck on a level and search on youtube on how to clear it, too bad, practically every video there is a "no kill, clean hands, undetected" who's requirements are to "Jump over there, blink on that pole, do 4 backflips, blink to that guard's head and invest in bitcoin" like dame, i am not going on a 4km journey just to get 40 coins. I got helped by maybe 1 guide all because some of those levels are build like maze. I have been given guns and crossbow, let me go on a killing rampage. Too bad, the game gets harder if you kill.

I absolutely loathe the chaos system. God forbid you kill an enemy that's about to kill you while bringing in more guards. I hate games that have concept of "face the consequences of your actions". I am playing this game to escape those consequences, why bring it back? The game practically punishes you for killing by increasing the number of weepers and guards along while making rats attack you.

The stealth was awful, all i have as weapons are a noisy gun and a crossbow. The sword legit carried the entire game. Some levels would be plain out impossible to be stealthy on, as guards spawn right in front of your face. Literally giving 0 time for hiding and if you get detected by even one of them, every guard and there mothers would come directly to your location.

From a story perspective, it was just plain out bad. The empresses dies, your daughter gets kidnapped and everyone blames you for it. The story goes to he…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes a chaos system that tracks player kills and modifies character reactions, story outcomes, and the number of enemies like weepers and rats.

citations.review_text:
i really hope Arkane can get back on their feet after what must be an incredibly scary time, especially after Arkane Austin got dissolved. if you want a good Arkane-ish game that takes the player's actions into account without openly condemning you or the game world for them, the best example out there is Prey (2017) or the original Deus Ex (but do not play deus ex revision i am begging you it is awful). speaking of, i want to articulate a criticism i've always had of dishonored:

dishonored still, in 2026, constitutes a breath of fresh air for the imsim/thief-y/looking glass-inspired genre of games. the world-as-designed is just overwhelmingly impressive, to the point where even things like electric viktor antonov trains dumping corpses into a hole feel so natural to this setting that it doesn't seem out-of-place.

as much fun as dishonored is to play (especially the Daud DLC's), there's one problem that still really hampers the experience in my opinion, which is the overbearing and quite nonsensical chaos system. like an honor/karma system from other games like mass effect or fallout (systems i also do not like), it tracks "good" and "bad" things you do, as judged by the developers, adding to a tally every time you kill an NPC, or occasional other things the game deems bad. gaining a high chaos rating has two effects:

1. the first effect changes your allies' perception of you - the allies that really matter, anyway. high chaos will make emily afraid of corvo, or cause billie to start murdering more people based on what she sees daud do (but she also thinks he's weak for killing people? that part doesn't quite work). this is the part that makes sense to me, because people are believably, you know, sensitive to whether their friend is a hyper-murderer or not. (whether corvo kills daud at the end of his second set of missions makes less sense, since he would have no way of knowing whether daud had changed)

2. the second effect, bizarrely, changes the entire state o…

I absolutely loved this game as a kid, I spent so much time just finding new creative ways to kill, incapacitate, sneak around enemies, and place bodies all around in funny ways to be seen or laughed at. The game holds up really well nowadays too, there are some parts that feel a little clunky like the hurdling when you blink to edges or when peaking. I’m not very good at stealth in all honesty, I’m more of a brute force a lot of times because I just suck at sneaking around and get impatient, I don’t remember the game being so strict on the chaos system you can only kill under 20% of each levels enemy count to be able to achieve a low chaos run, sometimes I would knock people out and they would die from falling or blowing up due to a trap but it’s fun to switch between hyper violent and non lethal play styles as well if you’re not concerned with canon endings, since your choices kinda don’t matter for the second game since it just asks you what chaos level you’d like to start at. I love the grungy sharp art style and the dingy and morbid environment with super dark storytelling, it just draws you into the environment so well, Corvo has such a great story to follow with a lot of fun and hedonistic characters that he meets, I’ve always found the story of Daud in the DLC way more impactful and interesting, he is a lot more intertwined with the myths of the world and the overarching narrative of the story than Corvo is when you play through it all the way and it’s so interesting to see what has been happening behind the scenes while you played through the main storyline and how it affects things, this game is super fun and I highly recommend it, it is one of the best stealth games I’ve ever played.

I came back to this game 10+ years after the my first playthrough. It's unbelievable how much BETTER the gameplay, the level design and the actual story is - compared to recently released AAA games.
It's awesome to experience the subtle differences in storytelling in low vs. high chaos mode and I loved to complete the challenges forcing me to use all my extra abilities and discover all the routes carefully planned by the designers.
I got goosebumps while playing the DLCs, it was like was watching a fantasy movie folding out in front of my eyes - while I was part of it!
I was so hooked, I just had to complete all the achievements too.
One of the rarest gem - thank you developers! ❤️

I enjoy this game so much.

The fact that I could get every skill available and not even use half of them depending on what style of play I'm going for is so cool. 

High chaos was painful at times, more weepers and rats isn't always easy to avoid and also the fact it changes the people around you as well. But it's so well done, I don't remember much from my low chaos playthrough but I do remember the feeling between both endings being SO different and I doubt I'll ever do high chaos again in this game.
the best stealth game ive ever played the combat, also the ending would be different based what your gameplay.this game also punished you for killing too many npc

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the Dunwall City Trials DLC presents extreme difficulty when attempting to complete achievements.

citations.review_text:
Another brilliant game by Arkane Studios

really enjoyed this game, still one of my fav stealth action RPGs that doesn't centre around horror, has it's moments here and there but as far as fine tuning this is one of the best attempts at a game with a compitent stealth system that's richly rewarding for people who want to go above and beyond. I think the gameplay still holds up and still has a really nice artstyle that captures the gloom and setting really well. Looking forward to playing the sequals. The only gripe i have is the Dunwall Trials DLC, If you're trying to 100% the game this DLC will drive you mad, apart from that i enjoyed this as well as the side story DLC for Daud. 8/10
whoever designed the achievements for dunwall city trias must be skinned alive

I've always heard great things about this game. I have to agree its incredible. Though I found myself remembering that it is both bethesda and a 2012 title with how often the collision jank threw me off. Definetely play it if you haven't already.

Edit: just finished 100% of all achievements, the story DLCs are incredible, adds a little spice to the gameplay that makes it feel fresh even after hours completing the base game achievements. The trials are a fun way to kill time if it weren't for how frustrating the achievements are to get. After nearly 100 hours still strongly recommend for both serious and casual players to try this masterpiece out.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the graphics have aged well and still look great due to the stylized art design.

citations.review_text: Truly one of the best games of all time in my opinion. The graphics are starting to show their age a tad, but the gameplay is still solid, and the world is just grimy enough that you'll want to get lost in it. Ahh, I can smell the butchered whale carcasses caressing my nose like a hobo with pie.

I first played Dishonored when it came out on Xbox. Almost 15 years later, it's still one of my favorite games of all time.

Dishonored has held up fantastically well, in regard to both gameplay and visuals. You have the freedom to make choices, and those choices greatly affect the story. The DLCs even further flesh out an already great story that's both cohesive and self-contained. Visually the game is very stylized--which I believe is a big reason it's held up so well--and it makes the worldbuilding even more believable.

If you enjoy any sort of FPS, stealth, or RPG gameplay, I cannot recommend Dishonored enough.

one of the most unique worlds in a video game and a system that allows for multiple ways to play. this is one of the most replayable games of all time. the graphics still look amazing thanks to the art style

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game can be glitchy, which makes the Dunwall City Trials challenging for achievement hunters.

citations.review_text:
I got this game on the Steam Summer Sale for $1.99 just thinking I couldn't pass up that kind of deal for a game that was on my radar. Well, 110 hours and a 100% completion playthrough later, it's fair to say I got my money's worth with this one haha. 

Pros:

-Some of the best stealth gameplay in the market hands down. Corvo (and another character in the DLC) feel amazing to play with and the Blink power does a lot of heavy lifting to make stealth feel truly your own and approach encounters in seemingly infinite ways. A highlight gameplay-wise for me was the final mission in the Brigmore Witches DLC as this mission really let you show your skills against some of the most dangerous enemies in the game. 

-I was surprised to see branching storylines in this game. You'll notice stark changes in dialogue and minor differences in gameplay depending on whether you wanna be a pacifist or go on a killing spree. In this way, Dishonored outdoes games that tout their ability to "change the outcome with your choices" without even using it as a selling point. 

Cons:

-The Dunwall City Trials are BRUTAL and not in the good way. This game can be a bit glitchy (its a Bethesda game lol) and this can really hamper the experience getting some of the rarest achievements in the game (Bonfires 3-star+Daredevil are atrocious in particular), which even if the game ran well are hard as hell. Completionists beware, you will bang your head into a brick wall trying to 100% this game.

I’d need to think long and hard before calling it my favorite game ever, but it’s absolutely in my top three. Dishonored was a turning point for me: the level design is phenomenal and still outclasses most modern games. The revenge plot isn’t your usual one either, it has some incredibly original peaks, helped by the mysterious and fascinating "Outsider".
The three ways to play the game have amazed me in every run, always revealing new little and hidden secrets. And once you master being either a total ghost or a brutal killing machine, you can pull off insanely fast routes or combos that feel amazing.
The intro is one of my all‑time favorites too, and the two Daud DLCs are fantastic for exploring his character in depth: motivations, growth, emotions.
Only downside: the challenge DLC, which is brutal if you’re going for the platinum. Everything else is basically infinite.
